claims.text: volforecast is a command line application: main in src/volforecast/__main__.py builds an argument parser, parses argv, and prints help when no subcommand is given.
The primary subcommand is run, which resolves a YAML experiment file into an ExperimentConfig, offering an interactive picker when no --config is supplied.

It is packaged with optional dependency groups, so the Goldman Sachs integration through gs-quant-internal and the machine learning stack through lightgbm, xgboost, optuna and shap are both installed only on request.
Every run reports what it produced through _print_output_summary, which takes an output directory and prints the resulting file paths.
It is not a live trading system or a service: nothing here listens on a socket, and every entry point is a batch command that runs to completion and returns an exit code.

claims.text: Imports of heavy dependencies are deferred into function bodies rather than done at module top level, which keeps the command line responsive and makes a broken optional dependency fail only the command that needs it.

Every CLI subcommand follows the same three function shape — register to declare the flags, handle to convert parsed arguments, and run to do the work — so a new command is added by copying that trio.
Cache writes go through a temporary file and an atomic replace, and the surrounding code merges rather than overwrites, so re-running an ingestion is expected to be safe.
Public functions carry numpy style docstrings with Parameters and Returns sections, and the deprecated path helpers are kept as thin aliases rather than deleted.
